item.title: Get Shit Done - SQSN — Tue Aug 4, 5:30 PM — 114 - living room
item.description:
This event is intended for Queer and/or Trans survivors:💜Some of the biggest barriers to survivor safety are finance related. While we do our best to put cash directly into survivors hands, in tandem, we thought it would be awesome to create a body doubling/coworking space where we can help each other executive function. 🤝 As well as offer relevant financial resources! That’s why we are launching “Get Shit Done” evenings🤓They will occur biweekly and be available in person or online. item.title: The Winks & Rouge Cabaret Burlesque and Drag Open Stage — Thu Aug 6, 8:00 PM — Durty Bull Brewing Company
item.description: Ready to unleash your inhibitions with a tantalizing twist burlesque and drag? Get ready for a night where desires ignite and fantasies come to life on our diverse, inclusive and queer friendly stage. From seasoned performers to fresh faces, we offer variety, diversity, and creativity for all. New to burlesque shows? This is the perfect place to start! Join us every first Thursday for a rendezvous where the daring and thrill seekers come to play. Here, tease is an art form, slow burn earns a new meaning, and every movement tells a story, even if it’s just “I’m Hot, look at me!”. It’s more than a stage; it’s community, love, and unity! Experience the art of tease and transformation as performers express themselves through their art. From seasoned artists with over a decade of experience to fresh faces just starting out, our stage celebrates variety, diversity, creativity and our doors are open to all styles, types, genders, and bodies. This is where you want to be on a Thursday night!

item.title: Future Fest Connect — Sat Aug 8, 9:00 AM — Durham Convention Center
item.description: Future Fest Connect is a gaming and technology expo designed to introduce school-aged students, college students, and early-career professionals to the world of game development and emerging technology. Through hands-on experiences, industry speakers, and interactive learning opportunities, attendees can explore career pathways in gaming, technology, and creative innovation. The event features the Epic Games Learning Lab, Durham’s First Indie Game Awards, independent game developers, resume and portfolio reviews by industry professionals, networking opportunities, and cutting-edge showcases—including a flying car. Future Fest Connect celebrates the future of gaming and technology by connecting developers, creatives, educators, and industry leaders with the community. Our mission is to bridge the gap between industry and community through gaming and technology by creating a space where ideas are shared, career questions are answered, and meaningful connections are built. item.description:
This is a three-hour class in which students will learn the basics of the copper foil or “Tiffany” method of creating stained glass. item.title: Incredible Science — Thu Aug 13, 1:30 PM — Downtown Raleigh
item.description:
Join us for an entertaining half hour of science experiments and demonstrations. Day-to-day topics vary but often include physics and chemistry demonstrations on inertia, buoyancy and electromagnetism. Enjoy natural science topics such as the incredible composition of beaver teeth or the amazing design and strength of birds’ eggs. This walk-up program is offered:
Wednesdays — 1:30pm Thursdays — 1:30pm Fridays — 1:30pm Saturdays — 12:30pm, 2pm
Location: Windows on the World on the 3rd floor of the Nature Exploration Center. Designed for ages 7 and up. No registration required.

item.title: Ballroom Barre Workshop with Lori Woods-Gay — Mon Aug 17, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Raleigh & Triangle Activities Meetup Group **Small group. Big improvement. Only 8 spots.**
#### What's this all about?
Ever wish your dancing just... clicked? Like your feet knew what to do without you having to think so hard about it? That's exactly what this workshop is for. Lori's running her signature **Ballroom Barre Workshop** — we'll use a ballet barre to really drill the fundamentals of Ballroom & Smooth dancing until they start to feel automatic. Less overthinking, more flowing. It's a **3-part series**, not just a single class, because muscle memory takes a little repetition to stick. Come to all three and you'll actually feel the difference by the end.
#### Is this for you?
Probably, if you:
* Know the basics but want your moves to feel more natural * Are working toward more advanced stuff and want a solid foundation first * Lead OR follow — this helps both * Don't have a partner — no problem, come solo!
#### When

item.description:

item.description:
Introducing, UNC Libraries’ AI platform, PromptLab! PromptLab is a user-friendly platform to interact with AI with no technical experience needed. You can use an assortment of open-source and cloud-based models, all managed by UNC and protected with institutional data safeguards. This workshop will teach you how PromptLab can support your teaching, learning, or work. Whether you’re an AI expert or an AI skeptic, this workshop will help you get started with PromptLab.
For more information, explore our PromptLab User Guide.
This workshop is offered by the University Library and will be led by Gracie Riehm.

item.title: Managing Your Research: Project Planning and Data Management for the Humanities and Social Sciences — Thu Aug 27, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Creating a project and data management plan is an essential component of planning your research project. This online workshop will cover the various phases of research for projects in the humanities and social sciences, creating a data management plan, and long-term preservation of your project and data. We will also include questions and considerations to keep in mind, such as technologies to use, seeking funding, publishing platforms, and more. By the end of the workshop, attendees will be prepared to begin planning their upcoming research project from research question development to preservation.
This workshop is offered by the University Libraries and will be led by librarians Rolando Rodriguez and Michele Hayslett.
This workshop is being offered remotely via Zoom. Register here: https://calendar.lib.unc.edu/event/17229771
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Creating Citations and Bibliographies with Zotero — Wed Sep 2, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Zotero is a free, easy-to-use tool to help you collect, organize, cite, and share research. Attend this session to learn how to manage your citations to make constructing your bibliography much easier. You’ll be able to import citations from research databases like Academic Search Premier or Scopus; use with word processing programs to insert citations into papers; create a correctly formatted bibliography; and use Groups to collaborate with other people. This class is structured for new to beginning users.
This workshop is offered by the University Library and will be led by librarian Rolando Rodriguez and CALA Shannon Henry.
This workshop is being offered remotely via Zoom. Register here: https://calendar.lib.unc.edu/event/17229826

item.title: beginR — Thu Sep 3, 12:30 PM
item.description:
Learning R on your own? Want some help along the way? beginR is a series of virtual meetings organized by the University Libraries and the Odum Institute that provides support to students, faculty and staff who are learning the R programming language. The first week, the instructors will introduce attendees to R, help them install the software, and share the materials that will be covered in subsequent meetings. In the following weeks, beginR attendees will learn R by following the lessons on the R Open Labs website at their own pace. Each week, staff will be available via Zoom to answer questions, solve problems and provide the solutions to exercises.
beginR is a collaboration between the University Library and the Odum Institute. The workshops will be led by librarians Lorin Bruckner and Matt Jansen, and Nuvan Rathnayaka from the Odum Institute.

item.title: Birding with Wake Audubon — Fri Sep 11, 8:00 AM — Williamson Farm and Nature Preserve
item.description:
Join TLC and Wake Audubon for this wonderful birding walk! Our wonderful partners at Wake Audubon have joined TLC to lead a hike on the second Friday of each month at our Williamson Nature Preserve. Join this wonderful morning stroll and see what birds you can find.
This hike will be just under 2 miles around the Two Pond Loop at the preserve. Please wear good walking shoes and layers, bring a water bottle, and binoculars if you have them. We suggest that you leave your furry friends at home for this hike as they may scare away wildlife viewing opportunities. This is a free event, but pre-registration is required.
If registration is full, please fill out the waitlist form here by September 10th at noon.
Inclement Weather Policy: In the event of inclement weather, you will be contacted by email for a call on cancellation or postponement.
Source: Triangle Land Conservancy

item.title: Moth Night — Sat Sep 12, 8:00 PM — Brumley South Nature Preserve
item.description:

This event is perfect for all ages and experience levels — whether you're a seasoned moth lover or just curious to learn more. Become a citizen scientist by bringing a camera or smartphone, sign up for a free iNaturalist account, and upload your nighttime discoveries. This event is free, but preregistration is required.
If registration is full, please fill out the waitlist form here by September 11th at noon.

item.title: ArcGIS Pro for Beginners — Tue Sep 15, 2:00 PM
item.description:
ArcGIS Pro is one of the most widely used GIS software platforms, with a range of applications that include business analytics, natural and health sciences, transportation, and more. Its suite of tools offers capabilities for analytics and data science, automation, data management and editing, image analysis, and artificial intelligence.
This hands-on course for beginners will provide an overview of ArcGIS Pro, including its layout and capabilities. Topics covered will include importing geographic data, styling and symbolizing data, querying and selecting data, making basic maps, and more!
Note: While everyone is welcome to join this workshop, we can only facilitate access to ArcGIS Pro for UNC-Chapel Hill affiliates.
This workshop is offered by the University Library and will be led by librarian Philip McDaniel.
This workshop is being offered remotely via Zoom. Register here: https://calendar.lib.unc.edu/event/17229080
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Making an Impact with Data Viz — Wed Sep 23, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Collecting data is now easier than it has ever been. But, as data becomes more prolific, datasets become larger and more complex. How do we find meaningful patterns in our data? How can we communicate those patterns to others? Data visualization allows us to make sense of today’s ever evolving information landscape.
This workshop will introduce the history and basic principles of data visualization. Learn about best practices and resources for making an impact with your data through compelling charts, graphs, and maps. At the end of the short course, participants will be able to:
Understand the preattentive process and how it affects visual perceptionCritically evaluate the accuracy and quality of visualizations they encounter in their daily livesImplement best practices when creating their own visualizations
This workshop is offered by the University Library and will be led by librarian Lorin Bruckner.

item.title: Exhibition – Reverence: Hair Memory Through Images — Thu Sep 24, 6:30 PM — The Sonja Haynes Stone Center for Research in Black Culture and History
item.description:
Jamaica Gilmer is a relentless hope-architect, multifaceted artist, and curator working across photography, ceramics, and film. Her most recent series, We are the Sun: A Photographic Tribute to Black Community, celebrates the intergenerational wisdom of ThirdSpace Action Lab in Cleveland, Ohio. She is the founder of The Beautiful Project (TBP) and the lead curator of TBP’s past exhibition at the Metropolitan Museum of Art’s Uris Center for Education, Pen, Lens, and Soul: The Story of The Beautiful Project. Her work is featured in Kleaver Cruz’s recent book, The Black Joy Project: A Literary and Visual Love Letter to How We Thrive. At the core of her organizing practice, Jamaica is committed to telling sacred stories of possibility through interdisciplinary making.
Read more about the artist: www.jamaicagilmer.com

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Tue Aug 4 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: NCMA Online Course for Educators: Art and Literacy — Tue Aug 4
item.description:
This self-paced course runs from Tuesday, June 16 to Tuesday, August 11. Participants can start any time between June 16 and August 4.
How can art be used to develop student growth in literacy skills? This self-paced online course explores methods for integrating art and literacy strategies to support North Carolina’s Literacy Instruction Standards across classrooms. Participants gain an understanding of how literacy is defined through a variety of lenses and apply their learning by developing a lesson plan. Strategies that incorporate NCMA works of art are used to practice and apply activities to build interpretive and expressive modes of literacy focused on a variety of reading materials, comprehension, vocabulary building, and writing. This course is designed for teachers of all disciplines and audiences. A certificate of participation for 20 hours will be provided for literacy, general, or content area credits (2 CEU, with prior approval from the local school system).
Source: NC

item.title: Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & The Fight for Independence — Tue Aug 4, 10:00 AM — Kings Mountain Historical Museum
item.description:
In partnership with the Catawba Cultural Center, Kings Mountain Historical Museum is excited to present, "Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & the Fight for Independence." This exhibit explores the critical role of the Catawba Nation, also known as Yį Iswąre or “People of the River,” in the American Revolutionary War, particularly in the backcountry regions of Tryon and Lincoln Counties. As skilled warriors, guides, and allies of the Patriot cause, the Catawba people defended their homeland, protected settler communities, and contributed to pivotal battles. Despite the hardships of disease, displacement, and warfare, the Catawba demonstrated extraordinary resilience. Their story is one of courage, alliance, and survival, woven into the struggle for independence in the Southern Campaign of the Revolution.
The exhibit will run from June 30, 2026 until October 24, 2026. Admission is Free!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.
Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.
Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. item.description:
May 2–August 9, 2026
East Building, Level B, Meymandi Exhibition Gallery
Knowing the West embraces and reexamines perceptions of the American West to create more inclusive and complex dialogues. The exhibition reflects the diverse perspectives that have contributed to art and life in the region. Presenting Native American works together with art by non-Native makers, it reveals how the stories we tell and the visual language we employ influence understanding of our nation’s history and cultures.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Wed Aug 5 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: NCMA Online Course for Educators: Art and Literacy — Wed Aug 5
item.description:
This self-paced course runs from Tuesday, June 16 to Tuesday, August 11. Participants can start any time between June 16 and August 4.
How can art be used to develop student growth in literacy skills? This self-paced online course explores methods for integrating art and literacy strategies to support North Carolina’s Literacy Instruction Standards across classrooms. Participants gain an understanding of how literacy is defined through a variety of lenses and apply their learning by developing a lesson plan. Strategies that incorporate NCMA works of art are used to practice and apply activities to build interpretive and expressive modes of literacy focused on a variety of reading materials, comprehension, vocabulary building, and writing. This course is designed for teachers of all disciplines and audiences. A certificate of participation for 20 hours will be provided for literacy, general, or content area credits (2 CEU, with prior approval from the local school system).
Source: NC

item.title: Spy Training 101: Decode a Secret Message — Wed Aug 5 — North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
item.description:
Pretend you’ve been recruited as a member of the Culper Spy Ring, and you need to know how to decipher a message written in invisible ink. Supplies include a paint brush, water, drying cloth, vitriol (diluted sulfuric acid), Thomas Jefferson cipher and “furnace box.” Read the clues to find the coin with a hidden message, reveal the message using the brush and vitriol, then use the cipher to decode the message.
Contact: Nancy Locquet Absillis, nancy.locquet@naturalsciences.org
Source: NC Cultural Resources
